# Expressing LP, QP/QCQP/SOCP, and Matrix Fractional Optimization as SDPs

## Preliminaries: SDP Forms

We use two equivalent SDP forms:

**Standard (primal) form:**
$$\min\ C \bullet X \quad \text{s.t.}\ A_i \bullet X = b_i,\ i=1,\dots,p;\quad X \succeq 0.$$

**LMI (epigraph) form:**
$$\min\ c^T x \quad \text{s.t.}\ F(x) = F_0 + \sum_{i=1}^n x_i F_i \succeq 0,\quad Dx = d,$$
where $F_i$ are symmetric matrices. These are equivalent: the LMI form is the dual of the standard form, and any LMI-form SDP can be converted to standard form by block-diagonalizing and dualizing. We use the LMI form throughout, as it is the natural language for these reductions.

**Key tool — Schur complement.** For $P \succ 0$:
$$\begin{pmatrix} P & Q \\ Q^T & R \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0 \iff R - Q^T P^{-1} Q \succeq 0.$$
For $P \succeq 0$ (semidefinite), the equivalence becomes:
$$\begin{pmatrix} P & Q \\ Q^T & R \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0 \iff R - Q^T P^{\dagger} Q \succeq 0,\ (I - PP^{\dagger})Q = 0,$$
but a cleaner device avoiding pseudoinverses is: for $P \succeq 0$,
$$x^T P x \leq t \iff \begin{pmatrix} t & x^T P^{1/2} \\ P^{1/2} x & I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0,$$
since the Schur complement of $I \succ 0$ gives $t - x^T P^{1/2} P^{1/2} x = t - x^T P x \geq 0$. Here $P^{1/2}$ is a constant matrix (the symmetric square root), so $P^{1/2}x$ is linear in $x$ and the block matrix is affine in $(x,t)$.

---

## (a) Linear Program as SDP

**LP:** $\min\ c^T x$ s.t. $Gx \preceq h$, $Ax = b$.

The componentwise inequality $Gx \preceq h$ means $h - Gx \geq 0$ entrywise, which is equivalent to the diagonal matrix being PSD:
$$\operatorname{diag}(h - Gx) \succeq 0.$$

This is an LMI with $F_0 = \operatorname{diag}(h)$ and $F_i = -\operatorname{diag}(G_{:,i})$ (the $i$-th column of $G$), so
$$F(x) = \operatorname{diag}(h) - \sum_{i=1}^n x_i \operatorname{diag}(G_{:,i}) = \operatorname{diag}(h - Gx).$$

**SDP formulation:**
$$\boxed{\min\ c^T x \quad \text{s.t.}\ \operatorname{diag}(h - Gx) \succeq 0,\quad Ax = b.}$$

This is an SDP in LMI form: the variable $x$ is free, the constraint is an LMI of size $m \times m$ (where $G \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$), and $Ax = b$ are linear equalities.

---

## (b) QP, QCQP, SOCP as SDPs

### Quadratic Program (QP)

**QP:** $\min\ \tfrac{1}{2}x^T P x + q^T x + r$ s.t. $Gx \preceq h$, $Ax = b$, with $P \succeq 0$.

Introduce epigraph variable $t$ and set $u = t - r - q^T x$ (affine in $(x,t)$). The objective constraint $\tfrac{1}{2}x^T P x \leq u$ is $x^T P x \leq 2u$, which by the Schur-complement device becomes:
$$\begin{pmatrix} 2u & x^T P^{1/2} \\ P^{1/2} x & I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0.$$

**SDP formulation:**
$$\boxed{\min\ t \quad \text{s.t.}\ \begin{pmatrix} 2(t - r - q^T x) & x^T P^{1/2} \\ P^{1/2} x & I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0,\quad \operatorname{diag}(h - Gx) \succeq 0,\quad Ax = b.}$$

The first LMI is of size $(1+n) \times (1+n)$ (where $P \in \mathbb{S}^n_+$); the second is $m \times m$ diagonal. All blocks are affine in $(x, t)$.

*(If $P \succ 0$, an equivalent single LMI using $P^{-1}$ is $\begin{pmatrix} P^{-1} & x \\ x^T & 2(t-r-q^Tx) \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0$, by Schur complement of $P^{-1}$.)*

### Quadratically Constrained QP (QCQP)

**QCQP:** $\min\ \tfrac{1}{2}x^T P_0 x + q_0^T x + r_0$ s.t. $\tfrac{1}{2}x^T P_i x + q_i^T x + r_i \leq 0$, $i=1,\dots,m$, with $P_i \succeq 0$ for all $i$.

Each quadratic constraint $\tfrac{1}{2}x^T P_i x \leq -r_i - q_i^T x =: u_i$ becomes, via the same Schur device with $u_i$ affine in $x$:
$$\begin{pmatrix} 2u_i & x^T P_i^{1/2} \\ P_i^{1/2} x & I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0.$$

The objective is handled with an epigraph variable $t$ and the LMI for $P_0$.

**SDP formulation:**
$$\boxed{\min\ t \quad \text{s.t.}\ \begin{pmatrix} 2(t - r_0 - q_0^T x) & x^T P_0^{1/2} \\ P_0^{1/2} x & I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0,\quad \begin{pmatrix} -2(r_i + q_i^T x) & x^T P_i^{1/2} \\ P_i^{1/2} x & I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0,\ i=1,\dots,m.}$$

This is a block-diagonal SDP: the full LMI is $\operatorname{diag}(M_0, M_1, \dots, M_m) \succeq 0$ where $M_i$ are the individual LMIs above. Convexity requires $P_i \succeq 0$ for all $i$; otherwise the problem is nonconvex and not an SDP.

### Second-Order Cone Program (SOCP)

**SOCP:** $\min\ f^T x$ s.t. $\|A_i x + b_i\|_2 \leq c_i^T x + d_i$, $i=1,\dots,m$.

The SOC constraint $\|u\|_2 \leq v$ (with $v \geq 0$) is equivalent to the LMI:
$$\begin{pmatrix} v & u^T \\ u & v I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0,$$
by Schur complement of $v$: $v I - uu^T/v \succeq 0 \iff \|u\|^2 \leq v^2$ (with $v \geq 0$ handled by the PSD condition forcing $v \geq 0$). Substituting $u = A_i x + b_i$ and $v = c_i^T x + d_i$ (both affine in $x$):

**SDP formulation:**
$$\boxed{\min\ f^T x \quad \text{s.t.}\ \begin{pmatrix} c_i^T x + d_i & (A_i x + b_i)^T \\ A_i x + b_i & (c_i^T x + d_i) I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0,\quad i=1,\dots,m.}$$

Each LMI is of size $(1 + k_i) \times (1 + k_i)$ where $A_i \in \mathbb{R}^{k_i \times n}$. The block-diagonal concatenation gives a single LMI. This shows SOCP $\subset$ SDP.

---

## (c) Matrix Fractional Optimization as SDP

**Problem:** $\min\ (Ax + b)^T F(x)^{-1}(Ax + b)$, where $F(x) = F_0 + \sum_{i=1}^n x_i F_i \succ 0$.

Introduce epigraph variable $t$:
$$\min\ t \quad \text{s.t.}\ (Ax + b)^T F(x)^{-1}(Ax + b) \leq t,\quad F(x) \succ 0.$$

Since $F(x) \succ 0$, apply the Schur complement to the block matrix $\begin{pmatrix} F(x) & Ax+b \\ (Ax+b)^T & t \end{pmatrix}$: the Schur complement of $F(x)$ is $t - (Ax+b)^T F(x)^{-1}(Ax+b)$, so
$$\begin{pmatrix} F(x) & Ax + b \\ (Ax + b)^T & t \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0 \iff t - (Ax+b)^T F(x)^{-1}(Ax+b) \geq 0,\ F(x) \succ 0.$$

The condition $F(x) \succ 0$ is automatically enforced: if the block matrix is PSD, then its principal submatrix $F(x) \succeq 0$; and if $F(x) \succeq 0$ but singular, the Schur complement condition $(I - F(x)F(x)^\dagger)(Ax+b) = 0$ must also hold, which combined with $t \geq (Ax+b)^T F(x)^\dagger (Ax+b)$ gives the correct extended-value extension. In the regime where the original problem is feasible ($F(x) \succ 0$), the equivalence is exact.

**SDP formulation:**
$$\boxed{\min\ t \quad \text{s.t.}\ \begin{pmatrix} F_0 + \sum_{i=1}^n x_i F_i & Ax + b \\ (Ax + b)^T & t \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0.}$$

This is a single LMI of size $(k+1) \times (k+1)$ where $F_i \in \mathbb{S}^k$. Every block is affine in the decision variables $(x, t)$: $F(x)$ is affine in $x$, $Ax + b$ is affine in $x$, and $t$ is a scalar variable. Hence this is a valid SDP, and its optimal value equals that of the original matrix fractional problem.

---

## Summary

| Problem | SDP LMI constraint | Size |
|---------|-------------------|------|
| LP | $\operatorname{diag}(h - Gx) \succeq 0$ | $m \times m$ |
| QP | $\begin{pmatrix} 2(t{-}r{-}q^Tx) & x^T P^{1/2} \\ P^{1/2}x & I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0$ | $(n{+}1)^2$ |
| QCQP | block-diag of objective + each quadratic constraint LMI | $\sum (n_i{+}1)^2$ |
| SOCP | $\begin{pmatrix} c_i^Tx{+}d_i & (A_ix{+}b_i)^T \\ A_ix{+}b_i & (c_i^Tx{+}d_i)I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0$ | $\sum (k_i{+}1)^2$ |
| Matrix fractional | $\begin{pmatrix} F(x) & Ax{+}b \\ (Ax{+}b)^T & t \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0$ | $(k{+}1)^2$ |

The unifying principle is the **Schur complement**: every convex quadratic/SOC/matrix-fractional constraint is the Schur complement of some affine block matrix, and thus each reduces to a single LMI. Since LP is the special case of an LMI with diagonal structure, all four problem classes are special cases of SDP.

## Preliminaries: SDP Forms

We use two equivalent SDP forms:

**Standard (primal) form:**
$$\min\ C \bullet X \quad \text{s.t.}\ A_i \bullet X = b_i,\ i=1,\dots,p;\quad X \succeq 0.$$

**LMI (epigraph) form:**
$$\min\ c^T x \quad \text{s.t.}\ F(x) = F_0 + \sum_{i=1}^n x_i F_i \succeq 0,\quad Dx = d,$$
where $F_i$ are symmetric matrices. These are equivalent: the LMI form is the dual of the standard form, and any LMI-form SDP can be converted to standard form by block-diagonalizing and dualizing. We use the LMI form throughout, as it is the natural language for these reductions.

**Key tool — Schur complement.** For $P \succ 0$:
$$\begin{pmatrix} P & Q \\ Q^T & R \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0 \iff R - Q^T P^{-1} Q \succeq 0.$$
For $P \succeq 0$ (semidefinite), the equivalence becomes:
$$\begin{pmatrix} P & Q \\ Q^T & R \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0 \iff R - Q^T P^{\dagger} Q \succeq 0,\ (I - PP^{\dagger})Q = 0,$$
but a cleaner device avoiding pseudoinverses is: for $P \succeq 0$,
$$x^T P x \leq t \iff \begin{pmatrix} t & x^T P^{1/2} \\ P^{1/2} x & I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0,$$
since the Schur complement of $I \succ 0$ gives $t - x^T P^{1/2} P^{1/2} x = t - x^T P x \geq 0$. Here $P^{1/2}$ is a constant matrix (the symmetric square root), so $P^{1/2}x$ is linear in $x$ and the block matrix is affine in $(x,t)$.

## (a) Linear Program as SDP

**LP:** $\min\ c^T x$ s.t. $Gx \preceq h$, $Ax = b$.

The componentwise inequality $Gx \preceq h$ means $h - Gx \geq 0$ entrywise, which is equivalent to the diagonal matrix being PSD:
$$\operatorname{diag}(h - Gx) \succeq 0.$$

This is an LMI with $F_0 = \operatorname{diag}(h)$ and $F_i = -\operatorname{diag}(G_{:,i})$ (the $i$-th column of $G$), so
$$F(x) = \operatorname{diag}(h) - \sum_{i=1}^n x_i \operatorname{diag}(G_{:,i}) = \operatorname{diag}(h - Gx).$$

**SDP formulation:**
$$\boxed{\min\ c^T x \quad \text{s.t.}\ \operatorname{diag}(h - Gx) \succeq 0,\quad Ax = b.}$$

This is an SDP in LMI form: the variable $x$ is free, the constraint is an LMI of size $m \times m$ (where $G \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$), and $Ax = b$ are linear equalities.

---

## (b) QP, QCQP, SOCP as SDPs

### Quadratic Program (QP)

**QP:** $\min\ \tfrac{1}{2}x^T P x + q^T x + r$ s.t. $Gx \preceq h$, $Ax = b$, with $P \succeq 0$.

Introduce epigraph variable $t$ and set $u = t - r - q^T x$ (affine in $(x,t)$). The objective constraint $\tfrac{1}{2}x^T P x \leq u$ is $x^T P x \leq 2u$, which by the Schur-complement device becomes:
$$\begin{pmatrix} 2u & x^T P^{1/2} \\ P^{1/2} x & I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0.$$

**SDP formulation:**
$$\boxed{\min\ t \quad \text{s.t.}\ \begin{pmatrix} 2(t - r - q^T x) & x^T P^{1/2} \\ P^{1/2} x & I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0,\quad \operatorname{diag}(h - Gx) \succeq 0,\quad Ax = b.}$$

The first LMI is of size $(1+n) \times (1+n)$ (where $P \in \mathbb{S}^n_+$); the second is $m \times m$ diagonal. All blocks are affine in $(x, t)$.

*(If $P \succ 0$, an equivalent single LMI using $P^{-1}$ is $\begin{pmatrix} P^{-1} & x \\ x^T & 2(t-r-q^Tx) \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0$, by Schur complement of $P^{-1}$.)*

### Quadratically Constrained QP (QCQP)

**QCQP:** $\min\ \tfrac{1}{2}x^T P_0 x + q_0^T x + r_0$ s.t. $\tfrac{1}{2}x^T P_i x + q_i^T x + r_i \leq 0$, $i=1,\dots,m$, with $P_i \succeq 0$ for all $i$.

Each quadratic constraint $\tfrac{1}{2}x^T P_i x \leq -r_i - q_i^T x =: u_i$ becomes, via the same Schur device with $u_i$ affine in $x$:
$$\begin{pmatrix} 2u_i & x^T P_i^{1/2} \\ P_i^{1/2} x & I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0.$$

The objective is handled with an epigraph variable $t$ and the LMI for $P_0$.

**SDP formulation:**
$$\boxed{\min\ t \quad \text{s.t.}\ \begin{pmatrix} 2(t - r_0 - q_0^T x) & x^T P_0^{1/2} \\ P_0^{1/2} x & I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0,\quad \begin{pmatrix} -2(r_i + q_i^T x) & x^T P_i^{1/2} \\ P_i^{1/2} x & I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0,\ i=1,\dots,m.}$$

This is a block-diagonal SDP: the full LMI is $\operatorname{diag}(M_0, M_1, \dots, M_m) \succeq 0$ where $M_i$ are the individual LMIs above. Convexity requires $P_i \succeq 0$ for all $i$; otherwise the problem is nonconvex and not an SDP.

### Second-Order Cone Program (SOCP)

**SOCP:** $\min\ f^T x$ s.t. $\|A_i x + b_i\|_2 \leq c_i^T x + d_i$, $i=1,\dots,m$.

The SOC constraint $\|u\|_2 \leq v$ (with $v \geq 0$) is equivalent to the LMI:
$$\begin{pmatrix} v & u^T \\ u & v I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0,$$
by Schur complement of $v$: $v I - uu^T/v \succeq 0 \iff \|u\|^2 \leq v^2$ (with $v \geq 0$ handled by the PSD condition forcing $v \geq 0$). Substituting $u = A_i x + b_i$ and $v = c_i^T x + d_i$ (both affine in $x$):

**SDP formulation:**
$$\boxed{\min\ f^T x \quad \text{s.t.}\ \begin{pmatrix} c_i^T x + d_i & (A_i x + b_i)^T \\ A_i x + b_i & (c_i^T x + d_i) I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0,\quad i=1,\dots,m.}$$

Each LMI is of size $(1 + k_i) \times (1 + k_i)$ where $A_i \in \mathbb{R}^{k_i \times n}$. The block-diagonal concatenation gives a single LMI. This shows SOCP $\subset$ SDP.

---

## (c) Matrix Fractional Optimization as SDP

**Problem:** $\min\ (Ax + b)^T F(x)^{-1}(Ax + b)$, where $F(x) = F_0 + \sum_{i=1}^n x_i F_i \succ 0$.

Introduce epigraph variable $t$:
$$\min\ t \quad \text{s.t.}\ (Ax + b)^T F(x)^{-1}(Ax + b) \leq t,\quad F(x) \succ 0.$$

Since $F(x) \succ 0$, apply the Schur complement to the block matrix $\begin{pmatrix} F(x) & Ax+b \\ (Ax+b)^T & t \end{pmatrix}$: the Schur complement of $F(x)$ is $t - (Ax+b)^T F(x)^{-1}(Ax+b)$, so
$$\begin{pmatrix} F(x) & Ax + b \\ (Ax + b)^T & t \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0 \iff t - (Ax+b)^T F(x)^{-1}(Ax+b) \geq 0,\ F(x) \succ 0.$$

The condition $F(x) \succ 0$ is automatically enforced: if the block matrix is PSD, then its principal submatrix $F(x) \succeq 0$; and if $F(x) \succeq 0$ but singular, the Schur complement condition $(I - F(x)F(x)^\dagger)(Ax+b) = 0$ must also hold, which combined with $t \geq (Ax+b)^T F(x)^\dagger (Ax+b)$ gives the correct extended-value extension. In the regime where the original problem is feasible ($F(x) \succ 0$), the equivalence is exact.

**SDP formulation:**
$$\boxed{\min\ t \quad \text{s.t.}\ \begin{pmatrix} F_0 + \sum_{i=1}^n x_i F_i & Ax + b \\ (Ax + b)^T & t \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0.}$$

This is a single LMI of size $(k+1) \times (k+1)$ where $F_i \in \mathbb{S}^k$. Every block is affine in the decision variables $(x, t)$: $F(x)$ is affine in $x$, $Ax + b$ is affine in $x$, and $t$ is a scalar variable. Hence this is a valid SDP, and its optimal value equals that of the original matrix fractional problem.

## Summary

| Problem | SDP LMI constraint | Size |
|---------|-------------------|------|
| LP | $\operatorname{diag}(h - Gx) \succeq 0$ | $m \times m$ |
| QP | $\begin{pmatrix} 2(t{-}r{-}q^Tx) & x^T P^{1/2} \\ P^{1/2}x & I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0$ | $(n{+}1)^2$ |
| QCQP | block-diag of objective + each quadratic constraint LMI | $\sum (n_i{+}1)^2$ |
| SOCP | $\begin{pmatrix} c_i^Tx{+}d_i & (A_ix{+}b_i)^T \\ A_ix{+}b_i & (c_i^Tx{+}d_i)I \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0$ | $\sum (k_i{+}1)^2$ |
| Matrix fractional | $\begin{pmatrix} F(x) & Ax{+}b \\ (Ax{+}b)^T & t \end{pmatrix} \succeq 0$ | $(k{+}1)^2$ |

The unifying principle is the **Schur complement**: every convex quadratic/SOC/matrix-fractional constraint is the Schur complement of some affine block matrix, and thus each reduces to a single LMI. Since LP is the special case of an LMI with diagonal structure, all four problem classes are special cases of SDP.
